subject: humanities
passage: Ajrak is a cotton cloth printed with carved wooden blocks in deep blue, red, and black geometric patterns, long worn as a shawl or turban cloth in Sindh, Pakistan, and in neighboring Kutch, India. During the twentieth century, many printers replaced the natural dyes indigo and madder with cheaper synthetic ones. In recent decades some workshops have returned to natural dyes, and textile historian Sana Memon argues that this revival has been sustained mainly by buyers outside the printers' home communities rather than by the local customers who have long worn the cloth.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Memon's argument?

choices.A: Natural-dyed ajrak fades more slowly than synthetic-dyed ajrak does when it is washed and dried in the sun.
choices.B: Workshops that returned to natural dyes now employ more printers and apprentices than they did when using synthetic dyes.
choices.C: Local customers account for most of the natural-dyed ajrak that these workshops sell in a typical year.
choices.D: Most natural-dyed ajrak goes to city shops and foreign buyers, while local customers mostly choose synthetic-dyed cloth.

explanation.why: Memon's argument is about who keeps the natural-dye revival going: outside buyers rather than local wearers. Support must compare who buys the natural-dyed cloth. If most of it goes to city shops and foreign buyers while local customers prefer synthetic-dyed cloth, the revival depends on outsiders.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A quality advantage might explain why anyone buys natural-dyed cloth, but it does not show which buyers sustain the revival.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Growth in the workshops shows the revival is doing well, not who is paying for it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. If local customers bought most of the natural-dyed cloth, the revival would rest on them, which weakens the argument.
explanation.D: Correct. Natural-dyed cloth is bought mainly by outside buyers, while locals mostly buy synthetic-dyed cloth, exactly as Memon argues.
